audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Null Sphere a silence, gives Riftwalk's cooldown as '2 seconds at 6 stacks' and 'six-second', and never mentions Nether Blade's auto reset, Force Pulse's charge mechanic, or Void Stone's magic-damage reduction.
audit.why: Riot text: Null Sphere deals damage, interrupts channels and shields Kassadin — no silence in the description and no silence flag in the kit. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s by rank, not by stack count. Nether Blade is a 7s auto-attack reset. Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1, a 400-range cone that charges off spells cast near him — including yours. Void Stone reduces the magic damage that is Swain's entire kit.
audit.corrected: Silence claims replaced with the shield and Void Stone; correct Riftwalk numbers written into whys[4], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and dosFull[0]; Nether Blade's reset tell and Force Pulse's charge added to breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: The missingInteractions entry claims Null Sphere is a channel that Nevermove cancels outright.
audit.why: That comes from a 'channel: interruptible' flag on Kassadin's Q, which is a tooltip-parse misfire — Riot's own description says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels; it is not itself a channel. Per the brief, the description wins over the flag.
audit.corrected: Claim NOT written to the page. Recorded here and in notes instead.

edits.before: His Q silence is his only answer to your E; throw E before Q so the bolt burst lands on a rooted, silenced-proof target and pull the Soul Fragment.
edits.after: Null Sphere shields him against your magic damage, so break the shield with Q bolts first, then E-root on the return sweep and pull the Soul Fragment.

edits.before: His Riftwalk cooldown at 6 stacks is 2 seconds — he is effectively untouchable; poke with W and collect cs, do not hard commit without a CC chain from your jungler.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and every repeat cast costs him more mana — poke with W, collect cs, and commit only with a CC chain from your jungler behind it.

edits.before: Full Kassadin silences you with Q before your E can root him, Riftwalks through your drain range, and one-shots before Demonic Ascension collects enough fragments to matter — respect the power curve and play grouped.
edits.after: Full Kassadin shrugs off your magic damage with Void Stone, Riftwalks out of drain range every 2s at rank 3, and bursts you before Demonic Ascension banks enough fragments — respect the curve and play grouped.

edits.before: Full Kassadin outruns and assassinates you — he Riftwalks inside your E range, silences you with Q, and kills you before Demonic Ascension can heal.
edits.after: Full Kassadin outruns and assassinates you — Riftwalk lands inside your E range, Void Stone cuts your magic damage, and he kills you before R can heal.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3 — his escape only scales, so kill him early. - Nether Blade: 7s auto reset; the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. - Force Pulse: 21s, 400-range cone, and every spell you cast near him charges it.

edits.before: Track Kassadin's Riftwalk: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. When it is down — E-root + W pull drain.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 — kill him before it hits 2s. Nether Blade's auto reset is the tell; step back on the wind-up.

edits.before: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3. Engage while it is spent, not after he blinks.

edits.before: Level 6 is his escape hatch, not yours. The moment Riftwalk is up he can blink out of your E mid-flight, break the root, and walk away from your R drain range. Shift to threatening with W poke on his farm path — the slow sets up an E root he cannot easily Riftwalk out of because he used it to approach. Do not chase after he blinks; reset, bank your fragments, and zone him off cs with W threat so he loses levels. If he uses Riftwalk aggressively to trade, Q-burst him when the six-second cooldown starts and force him back; his mana costs are brutal before Seraph's.
edits.after: Level 6 is his escape hatch, not yours. The moment Riftwalk is up he can blink out before your E sweeps back, break the root, and walk away from your R drain range. Shift to threatening with W poke on his farm path — the slow sets up an E root he cannot easily Riftwalk out of because he spent it approaching. Do not chase after he blinks; reset, bank your fragments, and zone him off cs with W threat so he loses levels. If he Riftwalks in to trade, Q-burst him inside the 5-second cooldown and force him back; each repeat cast costs escalating mana, and that is brutal before Seraph's.
